data.body:
Independent AC verification against merged `0033662b5534` ("Assert every EBS mount actually took"),
in a fresh worktree off `origin/main`. AC1-AC4 ticked on evidence. **AC5 left UNTICKED — it is not
met**, see below.

- **AC1 (F3) — HOLDS.** `replace_fstab_entry` in `infra/terraform/user_data.sh` rewrites by MOUNT
  POINT (`awk -v mp=... '$2 != mp'`, marked `# DROP-STALE-FSTAB-ENTRY`) and then appends the new
  line, replacing the old `grep -q "$uuid" /etc/fstab` append-if-absent guard.
  `test_replacing_a_volume_leaves_exactly_one_entry_for_the_mount_point` runs the exact T8
  scenario from this ticket (old `c814b8a1-…`, new `b1e23678-…`) and asserts exactly one entry
  afterwards, carrying the new UUID, with the unrelated `/` line intact.
  `test_rewriting_an_unchanged_volume_is_idempotent` covers the re-run case.
  Seeded: `test_removing_the_stale_entry_drop_restores_the_accumulation` drops the marked line and
  asserts the reported TWO-entry accumulation returns — so the guard is provably load-bearing.
- **AC2 (F3) — HOLDS.** `cp -p /etc/fstab /etc/fstab.rebar-bak` precedes the truncating rewrite,
  and `awk` reads the BACKUP and writes `/etc/fstab`, so the input is never the file being
  truncated. `test_the_previous_fstab_is_backed_up_before_it_is_rewritten` asserts the backup
  exists and is byte-identical to the pre-edit file. On-host and network-free by construction.
- **AC3 (F4) — HOLDS, and better than the AC asked for.** `chmod 0700 "$GATE_SCRATCH_MOUNT"` now
  precedes both `touch`es. The oracle is BEHAVIOURAL rather than a source-order assertion (the
  earlier comment on this ticket describes an order assertion; the landed test is not that):
  `test_the_markers_are_never_written_into_a_world_readable_mount_point` starts the mount point at
  0755, stubs `touch` to record `ls -ld | cut -c1-10` as it finds it, and asserts both markers were
  written at `drwx------`. Seeded:
  `test_removing_the_chmod_lets_the_markers_land_in_a_world_readable_directory` strips the `chmod`
  and asserts `drwxr-xr-x` is observed instead.
- **AC4 (F5) — HOLDS.** The nvme-cli branch now returns `readlink -f "$d"`, matching the by-id
  fallback. `test_both_resolution_branches_return_the_same_string_for_the_same_device` deliberately
  reproduces the sandbox shape (the globbed node is itself a symlink to the underlying device) so
  the test has teeth, then asserts both branches print the same string.
- **AC5 (F6) — NOT MET. Not ticked, and not tickable on the evidence.** Neither branch of the AC
  was delivered by this change, which does not touch `infra/terraform/variables.tf` or
  `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml` at all:
  1. `docker-compose.yml:268-269` still HARDCODES `REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR` / `TMPDIR` as
     `"/var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch"` — not derived from the terraform variable.
  2. `variables.tf`'s description still opens "Single-sourced here because four things must agree
     on it" — the inaccurate claim this AC exists to correct. It is true that the sentence already
     NAMES all four consumers, and true that `tests/unit/test_gate_scratch_volume_aa40.py` pins
     their agreement offline from one `SCRATCH_MOUNT` constant (verified: it asserts across
     `variables.tf`, both compose env vars, the compose bind, and `observability.sh`), so the
     silent-desync HAZARD is already gated. But AC5 asks for a *correction*, and no correction was
     made.

  No follow-up ticket exists for F6 — I searched the store and this ticket is the only hit. So the
  work is neither done nor tracked elsewhere; the deferral lives only in a comment.

Verification run in this worktree: `pytest tests/unit/test_user_data_device_resolution_d614.py
tests/unit/test_gate_scratch_volume_aa40.py` → **49 passed**. Shell gates clean:
`scripts/check_shellcheck.py` rc=0, `scripts/check_templatefile_escapes.py` rc=0. No production
host was touched, no terraform was applied, and no test was weakened to make a box tickable.
